findings_qualitative.value: No ordered motion on kpc scales in [CII] and CO(6-5); CO more centrally concentrated than [CII].

evidence.quote: No ordered motion on kilo-parsec scales was found in both \[C ii\] and CO(6-5) emissions.

claims.hypothesis: Does J0100+2802 host galaxy show ordered rotation and a dynamical mass consistent with the local M-sigma relation?
claims.experiment: Sub-kpc [CII] and CO(6-5) imaging, channel maps, virial mass
claims.result: No velocity gradient; sigma=161 km/s, ~3x lower than M-sigma expects
claims.finding: Gas not rotation-supported (or face-on); modest dynamical mass

evidence.quote: The velocity dispersion is measured to be 161$\pm$7 km s$^{-1}$, $\sim$3 times smaller than that estimated from the local M-$\sigma$ relation.

claims.hypothesis: Is the CO SLED of J0100+2802 described by a single or multi-component gas?
claims.experiment: RADEX LVG fits to CO(2-1) to CO(11-10)
claims.result: Single LVG poor; two components 24 K and 224 K
claims.finding: Highly excited gas, AGN heating possible

evidence.quote: which is best fit by a two-components model, including a cool component at $\sim24$ K

claims.hypothesis: Does the dust have different properties from typical z>6 quasars?
claims.experiment: Graybody fits and continuum ratio comparison
claims.finding: Dust hot and/or high emissivity; degeneracy unresolved

evidence.quote: which indicates that it has either a high dust emissivity $\beta\gtrsim2$ or a hot dust temperature $T_{\rm dust}\gtrsim60$ K

limitations_admitted.value: Continuum points lie on the Rayleigh-Jeans tail, so T_dust and beta are degenerate; shorter-wavelength data needed.

evidence.quote: most of the continuum points are on the Rayleigh–Jeans tail of the dust emission and we cannot tightly constrain the temperature and emissivity at the same time
